brief: Running a one-person company on an AI assistant

slots.subText: Six jobs a company would hire for, and what each one actually looks like when a model does the first draft instead.

slots.title: It writes the
slots.subtitle: The blank page is the expensive part, not the editing. A rough draft in thirty seconds changes what you are willing to start.
slots.b1Body: Fed enough of your past work, the draft sounds like you on a good day rather than like a press release.
slots.b2Body: Testing directions costs nothing, so you stop defending the first idea you had.
slots.b3Body: Reacting to a draft is a different cognitive task, and a far cheaper one.

slots.title: It clears the
slots.subtitle: Most messages need a decision, not a reply. Sorting them by what they actually ask for is the whole job.
slots.b1Body: The point of a forty-message thread, before you commit to reading it.
slots.b2Body: Drafted from the thread's context rather than a template you keep reusing.
slots.b3Body: Deadline pressure and social pressure look identical in an inbox. They are not.

slots.title: It replaces the
slots.subtitle: Twenty tabs half-read is not research. A structured comparison you can argue with is.
slots.codeComment: // find the signal before the opinion
slots.b1Body: Who exists, how they position, and where the actual gap is.
slots.b2Body: The thing repeated in four places that you would miss reading one at a time.
slots.b3Body: It ends in a decision with reasons attached, not a folder of links.

slots.title: It ships the
slots.subtitle: The internal tool nobody would fund is now an afternoon. That changes which problems are worth solving at all.
slots.codeComment: // the thing you would never have hired for
slots.b1Title: Scripts that would not survive a backlog
slots.b1Body: Too small to prioritise, genuinely useful every week.
slots.b2Body: Arguing over a working thing settles faster than arguing over a spec.
slots.b3Body: When building costs an afternoon, deleting it costs nothing either.

slots.title: Where it
slots.subtitle: Every one of these gains has a matching failure, and pretending otherwise is how people get burned.
slots.codeComment: // the part nobody puts in the thread
slots.b1Body: Fluency is not accuracy. Anything load-bearing still needs a person to verify it.
slots.b2Body: Left alone it produces the most likely sentence, which is rarely the interesting one.
slots.b3Body: It does not know which client is fragile or which decision is irreversible.

slots.title: What it did not
slots.subtitle: Six jobs got faster. The three that decide whether any of it matters did not move at all.
slots.b1Body: It answers questions well. Choosing which question matters is unchanged.
slots.b2Body: Relationships accrue to people over years and cannot be delegated.
slots.b3Body: It will produce competent work forever. Knowing when competent is not enough is the job.

slots.ctaBody: One person with this does the work of several. One person without judgement does the wrong work several times as fast.
slots.signoff: That distinction is the whole post
